page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.64-256 is an arm64 instance powered by the Ampere AmpereOne processor architecture. The configuration supplies 128 dedicated physical cores and 128 vCPUs clocked at a fixed frequency of 3.0 GHz. Because each physical core corresponds to a single execution thread, the architecture provides consistent core isolation without the resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 256.0 GB, which yields an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance configuration includes no bundled local NVMe or SSD storage, meaning disk operations require remote block volume attachments. Additionally, there are zero hardware GPUs integrated into this profile. Networking provision includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external ingress and egress routing.

The 1:2 memory-to-CPU ratio positions the VM.Standard.A2.Flex.64-256 primarily as a compute-optimized resource. Its architectural profile is well suited for high-throughput parallel compute tasks, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, containerized microservices, and general compute workloads that benefit from high physical core density on the 64-bit Arm platform.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.64-256 is an arm64 virtual instance configured with 128 dedicated physical cores and 128 vCPUs running on the Ampere AmpereOne processor platform at 3.0 GHz. Designed with a single execution thread per core, it eliminates hyperthreading contention across concurrent tasks. The system features 256.0 GB of total RAM, maintaining a compute-oriented allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no onboard local storage and no GPU acceleration, necessitating external block volumes for persistent data needs. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for basic network reachability. With its dense core layout and predictable execution pipeline, this server fits scalable compute workloads such as distributed application microservices, large-scale software builds, batch job execution, and parallel compute-bound tasks.
